engagement_title: Lumora lip oil shade range: seven shades built out of one physical sample, the gold collar held identical across all of them, the on lip detail proved on skin, the retailer's printed per shade shade cards run one record per page off the shade list, and the product page shade card and launch canvases handed back editable
vertical: Beauty and personal care: a direct to consumer colour cosmetics launch, one product in a seven shade range, sold shade first on mobile with a small retailer feed alongside
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-11 (Upwork). Its grounding_note, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Grounded in the Upwork hourly brief "Blind Box Packaging Design", PART A, PRODUCT PHOTO RETOUCHING. VERBATIM phrases quoted from the brief: "Clean up iPhone product photos I'll provide of one physical sample"; "Maintain consistent lighting, shadow, and gold-clasp detail across all"; "internal highlights and shadows should shift naturally with each color". The brief also asks to "Cut out the case on a transparent background, 300 DPI" and to "Recolor the case + wrist strap into additional color variants", and the identical real world intent is kept: one physical sample shot on a phone (here across'. Absorbs AO-114. The rebuild is needed because the ledger concept ended in a stack of recoloured tiles of one bottle, which is one deliverable rather than four, and sat on a single imaging surface. The fuller commission a launching beauty brand actually buys is the one here: the shade range built out of the sample so that the translucent oil, the shadow inside the bottle and the gold hardware all behave, the on lip detail proved on real skin rather than assumed from the glass, the transparent feed files the retailer requires, the shade card and launch canvases the brand edits itself between drops, and an honest reconciliation of what the sample can and cannot produce. The brand is the invented LUMORA and the shade names are coined; no real brand, retailer, manufacturer, platform or person is named.
client_one_liner: We made one physical sample and we are launching seven shades, so six of them have to exist as pictures, and the shade grid is the entire buying decision.
client_brief:
We are launching one lip oil in seven shades and we only had the budget to make one physical sample, so everything you are getting is that one bottle, Amber Hour, shot on a phone over an afternoon. Eleven frames on the white sweep, on a marble tile and held. Plus four on lip frames from the same afternoon with one model, same single shade.

We need the other six shades to exist as pictures. This is a twenty four dollar lip oil sold on a phone, and the shade grid is the entire decision the customer makes, so if one shade looks like a colour filter over a bottle then nobody trusts any of them.

Two things have to survive. The bottle has to be the same bottle in every shade: same light, same shadow under it, and the gold collar and the cap identical throughout, because that is the same part on every unit and if it drifts shade to shade it looks like seven different products from seven different factories. And the oil is translucent, so as the shade changes the highlight down the glass and the shadow inside the bottle have to move the way real oil would, not sit there like a sticker.

Where the pictures go. A shade grid on the product page. A hero tile per shade. An on lip detail per shade underneath the grid, because that is what people actually look at before they buy. A transparent version of every bottle for the retailer feed at the sizes in the file I sent. And a tall launch canvas plus a square announcement.

We have nothing shot in a room. If the launch canvas needs a surface behind it, buy one and bill us.

One more thing for the shops. The three boutiques taking us want a little printed shade card by each tester, one per shade, and their card printer sent over the card he already runs so we do not reinvent his layout. Run our seven shades through it off the shade list, one card per shade, each card showing that shade's own bottle and its name, its finish and the twenty four dollar price, at print resolution, and tell us honestly if anything cannot be made press ready with bleed from his file.

Give us the launch pieces as one file we can edit ourselves, because the drop dates change. Plus a note of what you dialled per shade, and an honest list of which shades you could genuinely make from the sample bottle and which ones we have to go and shoot.
price_band_and_audience: A 24 dollar lip oil bought by 18 to 32 year olds shade first on a phone, discovered on social and cross shopped against a 6 dollar drugstore oil and a 38 dollar prestige one. The band is load-bearing throughout. At 6 dollars the shade grid can be a flat swatch chart because nobody expects the picture to be the product. At 38 dollars the customer is buying reassurance and the imagery goes editorial, low key and styled. At 24 dollars the whole proposition is that it looks more expensive than it is while still looking honest, so the treatment is bright, clean and daylight neutral, with real glass, a real shadow under the bottle and hardware that looks like metal rather than like a gold coloured shape. That decides the grade, the ground, the crop and the type: a moody prestige treatment misprices the range upward and reads as a lie when the parcel arrives, while a blown out drugstore treatment kills the one advantage the brand has. The on lip detail carries the same rule, because a sheer oil pushed until it reads as a lipstick is the fastest possible route to a wrong shade return. The ledger records the base concept at 300 to 700 dollars; this fuller commission, with the on lip range, the retailer feed files and the editable canvases, runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer colour cosmetics: one lip oil launching in a seven shade range, sold shade first on mobile with a small retailer feed alongside.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2025, a two founder beauty startup based in Los Angeles, launching its first product.
brand_identity.about: Lumora is a new lip oil brand launching with one product in seven shades. We are shade led: the grid is the whole decision our customer makes on her phone. We made one physical sample and built the range around it, and we care that a shade looks like the oil it is rather than a filter over a bottle.
brand_identity.audience: 18 to 32 year olds discovering us on social and buying shade first on a phone, cross shopping a 6 dollar drugstore oil and a 38 dollar prestige one.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 24 dollar lip oil. We want to look more expensive than we are while staying honest, so the treatment is bright, clean and daylight neutral, never moody prestige and never blown out drugstore.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a clean confident sans with a little character; text in a neutral daylight sans. The feel is fresh and self assured, neither serif prestige nor bold discount.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, a bit fun, never overclaiming. We describe the finish and let the shade speak. Example line the brand would write: 'A sheer wash of colour, a proper shine, no stickiness.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and shade lockups exist as working digital files. There is no printed guideline; the carton photograph we have was shot under shop light and should not be trusted as a colour reference.
brand_identity.values: That the shade on the screen is the shade on the lip, and that a launch can look premium without pretending to be prestige.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_bottle_session/ (11 frames, 4032px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The one physical sample, Amber Hour, shot on a phone over an afternoon. Five on the white sweep, three on a marble tile, three held in hand." Clear glass bottle, translucent amber oil, gold anodised cap and brushed gold collar.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody at the brand can see. First, the sweep frames were lit from behind and the marble frames from the front, so in the backlit frames a specular ladder runs down the glass shoulder at almost exactly the oil's own value: a mask asked for the oil takes that ladder with it there and leaves it behind in the front lit frames, so one masked move lifts the highlight into a coloured smear on some frames and leaves a dead grey highlight on others, and both look plausible at grid size. Second, the gold collar and the cap both carry a warm reflection of the amber oil, so even a mask that holds only the oil leaves the hardware quietly belonging to the old shade, and any global temperature move shifts the gold itself.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_onlip_frames/ (4 frames, 4032px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Four on lip frames from the same afternoon, one model, the same single shade." Close crops of the mouth and lower face with the oil freshly applied.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A sheer oil over skin is a different optical object from the same oil in glass: the model's own warm lip tone reads straight through the film, so a shade move that lands correctly in the bottle lands somewhere else entirely on the mouth, and the ring light's reflection sits across the lower lip exactly where the colour reads, so any move that touches it either colours the reflection or flattens it. Which shades survive the transfer to skin is a property of this model's lip tone and this light, and nothing in the frames announces it.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_carton_flat.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A picture of the printed carton, in case you need our colours." A phone frame of the retail carton lying on a counter.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Shot under a shop fluorescent with the carton's gloss varnish throwing a bloom across the printed panel, so the colours in this picture are neither the carton's real ink nor the oil's real colour, and treating it as a colour reference sends the whole shade family off in one direction at once.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shade_list.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The seven coined shade names, the finish description for each, the product copy, the ingredient line and the launch wording for the tall canvas and the square.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_placements.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The product page grid and hero tile sizes, the retailer feed's transparency requirement and its stated pixel dimensions, and the grounds the tiles sit on, described in plain language.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shadecard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The little printed shade card the boutiques want by each tester. This is the card our retailer's printer already runs, one per shade." A single small portrait card: a bottle picture at the top, a round colour swatch dot beside the shade name, the shade name large, the finish line under it, the twenty four dollar price, and the ingredient line and tagline along the bottom.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card reads as tidy separate fields with a colour swatch well beside the name, but it is not set that way. The shade name, the finish line and the price are one continuous text story in a single frame, so the offset each field sits at has to be reconstructed from the story text rather than read off the mapping, and the sample was built for the one physical shade so that story leads with the baked word Amber Hour. The round swatch dot that reads like a colour chip well is a decorative spot colour vector group, not a picture frame, so the only real graphic frame on the card is the bottle well. And the card is trim only at 55 by 85 mm: a PDF converted into InDesign through convert_pdf_to_indd carries no bleed box at all, because the connector sets the bleed box equal to the trim box, so no press ready with bleed card can be produced from this template however the bottle is placed, and the honest deliverable is the card at trim with the bleed shortfall reported.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_shadecard_merge.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The seven shades as one row each for the card run: shade name, finish line, price, a swatch note and a picture column pointing at the per shade bottle picture to bind.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rows are not in the shade list's order, so row one is not Amber Hour and a card cannot be named by its position in the run. One name drifts from the list, Mulberry Dusk written as Mulberry, so a card named or bound off the raw cell disagrees with the range. Prices are written inconsistently across rows even though they are all twenty four ($24, 24.00, 24). The near clear shade Clear Dawn has a blank picture cell that no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, because there is no distinct swatch for a barely there wash. And Coral Flash's picture cell points by copy paste error at Peach Noon's cut file, so a naive bind prints Peach Noon's bottle on the Coral Flash card.

acceptance_bar: Every shade tile reads as translucent oil in glass: the highlight down the shoulder and the shadow inside the bottle move with the shade rather than sitting on top of it, and nothing reads as a colour laid over a bottle shape.
The bottle is the same bottle in all seven tiles: same light, same shadow under it, same position of the shadow's edge.
The gold collar and the cap are identical across all seven tiles and have not drifted with any shade move.
The seven read as one range when the grid is viewed at the size the product page actually shows it, not only at full size.
Each on lip detail matches its own bottle tile when the two are placed together, and no on lip frame has been pushed until the sheer oil reads as an opaque lipstick.
The transparent feed files carry genuine transparency at the stated pixel dimensions, with a clean edge on glass and on the gold hardware, judged on the retailer's own ground rather than on white.
No delivered file exceeds its source dimensions and nothing carries invented pixels, with every resize or edge extension any tool reported listed in the note.
All four canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the brand also gets the self contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the brand can retype, the shade card's grid is a real table rather than a picture of one, and every photograph in it is embedded rather than referenced.
Anything licensed sits with the brand's own photography rather than reading as a bought surface with a bottle placed on it.
One type system across the shade card and the canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The review board carries the finished range with nothing silently missing from it.
The note states per shade what was applied, and gives an honest list of which shades the sample bottle can genuinely produce and which the brand has to go and shoot.
Nothing in the delivered set was colour matched off the carton photograph.

The retailer's shade cards are produced as one record per page, page count equal to the shade count, each card carrying its own shade's name, finish and price and its own shade's cut bottle picture, rendered at 300ppi at trim.
Every shade card proof is named from what is actually inside it, no two proofs share a name, and no card shows one shade's name over another shade's bottle picture.
The near clear shade's card, whose picture cell is blank, is handled deliberately rather than left as a hole, and the drifted shade name is reconciled to the range's own name.

The shade cards are delivered at trim (55 x 85 mm) and nothing is claimed as press ready with bleed, because a PDF converted into InDesign carries no bleed box (BleedBox = TrimBox), and the bleed shortfall is reported honestly in the note.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the range and the cut outs on imaging, the shade card and the three canvases on HTML authoring.
trajectory.judgement: The obvious reading is that this is a recolour job with a layout on the end. The actual structure is that the range has to survive two different optical situations (glass and skin) and two different grounds (the product page and the retailer feed), and one deliverable is defined by still being editable at the next drop.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eleven bottle frames, the four on lip frames and the carton picture, holding a manifest with source dimensions per file.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no invented pixels claim later is made against them, and phone frames leave very little headroom.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions and a presigned URL per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all fifteen frames and triage: lighting direction per frame, where the specular sits on the glass, how much of the bottle each frame gives, and which frames can plausibly carry a shade tile at all.
trajectory.judgement: The carton picture is the trap here. It is offered as a colour reference and it is the one asset that cannot be used as one, and deciding that early is what keeps the whole family from being pulled off in one direction.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note and a stated decision about the carton picture.

trajectory.action: Straighten where the handheld frame is off, then fix one look on the strongest sweep frame and correct the rest toward it, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: The three lighting situations need genuinely different corrections to arrive at the same place, which a single batched parameter set cannot do. The band rules out a moody prestige grade and a blown out drugstore one alike.
trajectory.produces: Fifteen corrected masters with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole frame move is wrong: correct the white sweep and the glass separately by naming the material rather than the product.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the product returns the bottle as an object and takes its shadow with it; naming the material returns what is actually needed. The sweep and the glass want opposite moves.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the sweep grey or the glass green.

trajectory.action: Build the oil only mask on the chosen hero frame by naming the oil's own visual properties, then dial the six additional shades with masked adjustments, one parameter set per shade, logging every one.
trajectory.judgement: How far a translucent amber can be carried and by which class of move is the craft. An adjacent hue move, a desaturate and darken move and a lift toward a pale neutral are three different operations, and applying the wrong one produces a plausible looking tile that is not the shade on the list.
trajectory.produces: Seven shade masters with a full parameter log.

trajectory.action: Place the seven tiles at the product page grid's delivered size beside the base frame and inspect the highlight down the glass shoulder and the shadow inside the bottle on each.
trajectory.judgement: A shade tile judged at full size always looks fine. The grid size is where the customer sees it and where the specular either behaves or does not, and deciding to look there is the agent's own move.
trajectory.produces: A per shade verdict on the highlight and the internal shadow at grid size.

trajectory.action: Check the gold collar and the cap across all seven and correct by mask anything that has travelled, rather than by a further global move.
trajectory.judgement: The hardware is the same physical part on every unit, so any drift is a manufacturing lie. It is also the thing a global temperature correction moves first, which is exactly why the correction has to be masked.
trajectory.produces: Seven tiles whose hardware is identical, with the corrections recorded.

trajectory.action: Carry the shade decisions onto the on lip frames, then lay each on lip detail directly beside its own bottle tile at the size the product page shows the pair.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the only place a mismatch exists. Judging an on lip frame alone always passes, because a plausible lip is a low bar; judging it against its own bottle is what the customer does.
trajectory.produces: An on lip detail per shade and a paired verdict against each bottle tile.

trajectory.action: Produce the retailer feed cut outs with genuine transparency at the stated pixel dimensions, and the product page plates on the site ground in one operation where the frame allows it, holding png through the whole chain.
trajectory.judgement: Glass and polished gold are the hardest possible subject for an automatic knockout, and the one call ground route and the select, invert and fill route are not interchangeable. A single jpeg step anywhere in the chain destroys the alpha the feed depends on.
trajectory.produces: Transparent feed files and site plates across the range.

trajectory.action: Compose the hero, grid and feed crops at the sizes each is actually used at, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata, and extend a frame at its edges rather than interpolating it where a placement needs more room than the phone frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: A grid thumbnail and a hero tile are not the same crop scaled, and a phone frame has almost no headroom. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated, and adding edge material is the only route that does not invent detail.
trajectory.produces: Composed crops per shade with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a surface or setting frame for the tall launch canvas, filter to photography, exclude generated results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the range's light and lay it beside the graded tiles.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to the range's rather than the best thumbnail, and then judging whether it sits with the brand's own phone shot photography or reads as a bought still life with a bottle placed on it. A 240 pixel thumbnail is not evidence about light.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale surface frame, graded and judged against the range.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read at 24 dollars: confident and clean rather than prestige serif or drugstore bold. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and the CSS must use the returned stack.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes: the shade card whose grid is a real table with a swatch tile and a name per cell, the PDP hero module, the tall launch canvas and the square announcement. Embed every photograph as image data and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is showing seven shades without the page turning into a paint chart.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole set, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest, asserting that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the shade grid arrived as a real table with per cell content, and that nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with four canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the card printer's shade card template PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, what each one holds, and whether the file carries a bleed box.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how it was set. The colour swatch dot that reads like a chip well may not be a picture frame at all, and the tidy separate fields may be one continuous story. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly: a PDF converted through convert_pdf_to_indd carries no bleed box (the connector sets the bleed box equal to the trim box), so the honest verdict is that the cards can only be delivered at trim and no press ready with bleed is producible from this template.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, a bleed verdict, and a mapping strategy chosen from what is actually there rather than from what the printed card implies.

trajectory.action: Cut a card bottle picture per shade from the graded shade masters to the card's proportion and place each on the soft cream card ground so it reads on the card's own ground rather than as a transparent centred cut, reading what each crop reports, and reconcile the set against the shade list including the near clear shade whose swatch cell is blank.
trajectory.judgement: The card run sends the job back to imaging: the merge binds a real picture per row, a transparent centred cut would float on the frame rather than sit on the card's ground, and a blank picture cell is not an error the merge raises, so what a barely there shade's card looks like is decided here rather than found on the printed sheet.
trajectory.produces: A per shade card picture on the card ground, a stated treatment for the near clear shade, and the picture to shade reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the template's true story text from the interchange file, compute every field offset from that string past the baked Amber Hour lead, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re export and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened or wrongly assumed string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed where the shade name, finish and price each begin is finding it in the re exported document, and the swatch dot must not be mapped as a picture because it is not one.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Run the seven shade rows against the template binding each row's own card picture through the prefixed picture column, produce the printer's run at print resolution and a proof per shade, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, the row order does not match the shade list so position names nothing, the drifted name and the copy paste picture cell have to be caught, and a file's place in a returned list is not evidence of which shade is inside it.
trajectory.produces: The seven card run plus a proof per shade, each verified against its shade row.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished range and the shade card proofs for the founder and the retailer buyer, treating a partial success as partial and re sending only what failed. Then write the note: per shade what was applied, the honest list of which shades the sample can produce and which have to be shot, why the carton picture was not used as a colour reference, the type system, what was licensed, that the shade cards are delivered at trim because a PDF converted into InDesign carries no bleed box to make them press ready with bleed, and every resize or extension any tool reported.
trajectory.judgement: The honest list is the part the brand will act on before it commits to a fill run, and it has to name the shades plainly rather than leave a wrong colour to be discovered by a customer who returns it, on the shelf card as much as on the screen.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the mask behaves on this particular glass. In the backlit sweep frames a specular ladder runs down the bottle's shoulder at almost exactly the oil's own value, so a selection aimed at the oil takes it with it; in the front lit marble frames the same wording leaves it behind. The consequence only exists after the shade move is applied: on one set of frames the highlight picks up the new shade and turns into a coloured smear where a real oil would keep a near neutral specular, and on the other the highlight stays where the old amber left it and reads dead against the new shade. Both come back reported as success, both look entirely plausible at full size, and the difference only shows at the size the product page grid actually renders the tile. Selection masks return with no intermediate values at all, so there is nothing about the mask itself to inspect that would predict it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it: which wording captures the specular is a property of this bottle, this oil's density and the direction the light came from in each frame, there is no measurement of any kind available, and the mask carries no edge information to read. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the highlight and the internal shadow have to move the way real oil would, which is the client naming her standing requirement exactly as she would to a retoucher, not a disclosure that any frame will misbehave or which ones. No asset note names a frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a second selection aimed at the specular itself so it can be held back or moved on its own terms, or a partial opacity fill through a separate mask instead of an adjustment, or dropping the backlit frames from the grid entirely, which changes which frame carries which shade.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Split the mask so the specular is treated on its own terms rather than pushing the same adjustment harder, or move the shade with a partial opacity fill through a second selection, then re place the tiles at grid size and look again rather than assuming the second route took. Inspect the shades that were not flagged at the same size, since the reason to look was found on one tile and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not behave, move the shade it was carrying to a frame that will and re compose that tile's crop.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The product page shade grid, which is the entire buying decision at this price, shows several shades whose highlights are stained the colour of the oil and others whose highlights are grey, so the range reads as retouched rather than photographed and every shade in it loses credibility at once.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the shade decisions that are right in glass are right on skin. A sheer oil over a mouth is a different optical object from the same oil in a bottle: the model's own warm lip tone reads straight through the film, so a move that lands a shade correctly in glass lands somewhere else on the lip, and the ring light's reflection sits across the lower lip exactly where the colour is read, so a move that touches it either tints the reflection or flattens the lip into something opaque. How far each shade travels between the two is a property of this model's lip tone and this light. Nothing reports it, the on lip frame comes back looking like a perfectly plausible lip, and the mismatch only exists when the on lip detail is placed beside its own bottle tile, which is exactly how the product page shows them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it: the comparison needs both the bottle tile and the on lip frame to exist, and a plausible lip is not evidence that the shade matches its bottle. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for an on lip detail per shade because that is what customers look at, which is the client describing a placement, not a claim about optics, and the honest list she asks for is explicitly bounded to which shades the sample bottle can produce. No asset note and no acceptance line names the transfer to skin. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix is a different class of move on skin than in glass, a separate parameter set per shade for the on lip frames, or a decision that a shade's on lip detail is carried by a different one of the four frames, none of which is the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Dial a separate set of parameters for skin rather than reusing the glass ones, aim a selection at the film on the lip rather than at the lip, hold the ring light reflection out of the move, then place each pair together again and judge the pair rather than the lip. Where a shade will not transfer at all, decide which of the four on lip frames carries it and re compose that detail crop around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Under every shade in the grid sits an on lip picture in a visibly different colour from the bottle above it, which is the single fastest route to a wrong shade return and to a review saying the swatches are fake.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed frame can sit under this range at all. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail, and the frame's true white balance, its true neutral and how hard its own light falls only exist once it has been licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward the range's look. Two candidates that look equally bright and equally simple at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution, and the specific risk at this band is not that a frame is bad but that it is too good: a professionally lit still life surface sits under a phone shot bottle and immediately announces that the bottle was placed on it, which is only visible with the licensed frame and the finished tiles laid out together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished range to exist, and it cannot be settled by care, because a 240 pixel thumbnail carries no information about light. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that there is nothing shot in a room and that a surface can be bought if it is needed, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The likely response is to abandon the frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, or to give up on a bought surface and extend one of the marble frames at its edges instead, which changes the launch canvas's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward the range's light, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the light the range actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re grade it, then lay the range out again and judge the whole set rather than checking the new frame alone. If nothing joins, extend one of the brand's own marble frames at its edges and re compose the launch canvas around the room that produces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The tall launch canvas that carries the whole drop reads as a stock photograph with a product cut out dropped onto it, which at 24 dollars reads as a brand that could not afford to photograph its own product, in the exact placement chosen to say the opposite.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered shade card actually carries the shade its filename claims. The natural way to hand the boutiques a proof per shade is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and returns a list labelled by row number. The labels are not to be trusted: multi record raster output comes back in an order that does not match the roster and nothing in the response says so, and on top of that the merge rows are not in the shade list's order to begin with, one name is drifted, and one picture cell points at the wrong shade's cut. Every gate above passes, the count is seven, each file is a valid card, and the only way to learn any of it is to open the cards and read the shade name and the bottle picture inside each against the row it was named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and no parameter controls it, because the mis ordering is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files, while the copy paste picture cell and the drifted name are facts about this data that only surface when the rendered card is read. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about each card carrying its own shade's name and bottle is the retailer's requirement, and the brief never characterises how the run comes back. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page render whose page order is trustworthy or a per record recordRange loop producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, plus a return to the data to correct the drifted name and repoint the mis pointed picture cell.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re run the card set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, correct the drifted shade name to the list's canonical Mulberry Dusk and repoint Coral Flash's picture cell to its own shade's cut, decide and place the near clear shade's card, then rename every proof from what is actually inside it and read each card against its shade row again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A shelf of tester cards where the card that says Coral Flash shows the Peach Noon bottle and a card carries a name the range does not use, printed and clipped by each tester, so the one printed piece a customer holds in the shop tells her the wrong shade, which at 24 dollars is a wrong shade return and a public review that the swatches are fake.

deliverables.name: Lumora shade range, seven bottle tiles and seven on lip details at one look
deliverables.spec: Fifteen phone frames from three lighting situations brought to one clean daylight look, and six additional shades built out of the single physical sample so that the highlight down the glass, the shadow inside the bottle and the shadow under it all move with the shade, with the gold collar and cap identical throughout, paired with an on lip detail per shade that matches its own bottle tile on real skin. Delivered at the hero and grid crops composed for the sizes each is actually used at, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per shade parameter log and every resize or edge extension any tool reported.

deliverables.name: Retailer feed cut outs and product page plates
deliverables.spec: Each shade delivered as a transparent file at the retailer feed's stated pixel dimensions, with genuine partial alpha and a clean edge on both the glass and the polished gold hardware, judged on the retailer's own ground rather than on white, and as a plate on the product page ground produced without a jpeg step anywhere in the chain. Where a frame cannot be cut cleanly at the hardware, it is named and the shade it was carrying is moved to a frame that can.

deliverables.name: Shade card, PDP module, launch canvas and announcement as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document carrying a product page shade card whose grid is a real table with a swatch tile and a shade name per cell, a PDP hero module, a tall launch canvas and a square announcement, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system and every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, since the drop dates change.

deliverables.name: Retailer per shade shade card run
deliverables.spec: The card printer's flat press PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re exported document and the decorative swatch dot correctly not mapped as a picture, then run against the seven shade rows: the printer's run at print resolution (300ppi at trim) with page count equal to the shade count in roster order, each card binding its own shade's cut bottle picture on the card ground and carrying that shade's own name, finish and price, plus a proof per shade named from what is actually inside it rather than from a returned list order, with the near clear shade whose picture cell is blank handled deliberately, and the cards delivered at trim with the bleed shortfall reported honestly because a PDF converted into InDesign carries no bleed box to make them press ready with bleed.

deliverables.name: Shade reconciliation, handover note and review board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per shade what was applied, an honest list of which shades the single physical sample can genuinely produce and which the brand has to go and shoot, a plain statement of why the carton photograph was not used as a colour reference, the type system by role with foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, whether anything was licensed and why, and every resize or edge extension any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the finished range for the founder and the retailer buyer to sign off, with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Whether the carton photograph is usable as a colour reference, and what to do instead once it is ruled out.
Which of the fifteen frames can carry a shade tile at all, and which lighting situation the range's one look is built from.
Whether to word a selection at the product or at the oil, knowing the two return completely different masks and only one of them can carry a shade.
Which class of move each shade needs, and whether the specular needs a selection of its own rather than riding along with the oil.
Whether a shade that will not come out of the sample is pushed harder, produced a different way, or declared unproducible in writing.
Whether the gold hardware is corrected by mask or left alone, given that every global move touches it first.
Whether the on lip frames get their own parameter set per shade, and which of the four frames carries which shade.
Knockout route per frame rather than per range, given glass and polished gold, and on which ground the edges are judged.
Whether to extend a phone frame at its edges or accept a tighter crop, knowing extended material has to match the brand's own ground.
Whether a licensed surface joins the range or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it, search again on the light, or abandon it for an extended frame of the brand's own.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged at 24 dollars rather than at either end of the category.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a launch where a wrong shade becomes a return and a public review.
Whether the shade card template's swatch dot is a real picture frame or a decorative device, and where the per shade bottle picture actually binds given only the bottle well is a real graphic frame.

Which delivery route carries per record identity safely for the seven card run, given multi record raster output comes back reversed while labelled by row and the rows are out of the list's order, and what a card for the near clear shade with no swatch picture looks like.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a bottle that is not this bottle. IDENTITY is the commission: this is one physical sample the brand has actually tooled, with a specific glass profile, a specific brushed collar and a specific anodised cap, and a customer who receives a bottle that does not match the tile returns it and says so publicly. A regenerated shade is a guess about a fill the brand has not made yet. SPEC: the retailer feed wants genuine transparency at stated pixel dimensions with a clean edge on glass and polished metal, the product page wants a grid tile and a hero composed at the sizes they are used at, every on lip detail has to correspond to a real application of a real oil on a real mouth, and nothing may exceed its source resolution, which on phone frames is a hard ceiling. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, four canvases in one document the brand changes every drop, with live text and a shade grid that is a real table rather than a picture of one. And the middle of the job is verification against material reality: does this mask take the specular with it, does this shade survive the move from glass to skin, does this licensed surface sit under a phone shot bottle. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest list of what the sample cannot produce is professional advice a render cannot give. And the retailer's shade cards are a genuine one record per page run: seven cards, page count equal to the shade count, each bound to that shade's own picture and printed with that shade's own name, where a card that prints the wrong shade's bottle is a physical wrong shade lie a customer holds in the shop, which is a merge and a verification problem against a printer's own file, not a generation one.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted and deliberately not padded: the retailer's per shade shade cards are a genuine one record per page run so the InDesign layout merge surface is invoked rather than manufactured, while the Illustrator vector merge is still never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host, and no video or audio tool is touched for the same reason. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, auto_tone, auto_straighten, select_by_prompt and select_subject with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area with a mask and a percentage opacity, remove_background in both the transparent and the backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array and generative_expand are all verified headless. The masked colour variant system (one mask, N variants, different hslHue / hslSaturation / hslLightness per variant, the agent reporting what it dialled) is a verified collateral unlock, and the documented finding that HSL range holds at moderate is why the shade range is designed as adjacent hue moves and desaturate and darken moves rather than as jumps to named hexes. The prompt wording asymmetry (naming the object returns the object and its substrate, naming the material's own visual properties returns the material) is a verified live finding and is the entire gate on the oil only mask. Selection masks are verified to come back fully binary with zero intermediate values, which is why nothing about the mask predicts the specular behaviour and why the first checkpoint cannot be pre empted. image_apply_color_overlay is deliberately never used, because it takes no mask and no opacity; the percentage route is image_fill_area through a mask, exactly as that tool's own doc directs. Transparent RGBA with genuinely feathered partial alpha is verified and survives both crop tools at png output, and the documented rule that outputFileType must stay png through the whole chain is why one jpeg step would destroy the retailer feed files. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, and remove_background is documented as silently downscaling oversized inputs and reporting it only as a tradeoff, so the no invented pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than as any measurement the agent takes, which matters more here than usual because 4032px phone frames have almost no headroom. No hex is ever read: the agent works by eye and reports the parameters it applied, and the swatches in the shade card are cropped tiles of the recoloured oil rather than colour values, so nothing in the task requires an eyedropper that does not exist. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator pass, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution are verified fully headless and synchronous, with one record per page for a PDF derived template and page count equal to row count, so the seven shade rows produce seven cards at print resolution. The card identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record PNG and JPEG output comes back REVERSED while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes, so per shade identity is scored by reading the rendered card rather than by trusting the returned order. The reverse engineering trap rests on the verified facts that what a converted PDF exposes as frames is unrelated to how the printed sample reads, that a decorative vector group is not a picture frame and must not be mapped as one so the only bindable graphic frame is the bottle well, and that generate_indd_mapping_prompt validates offsets against whatever story string it is given, so a field only counts as landed once it is found in the re exported document. PDF derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and convert_pdf_to_indd carries no bleed at all (BleedBox = TrimBox = MediaBox), so no press ready with bleed can be produced from this template; the cards are delivered at trim and the bleed shortfall is reported honestly rather than asserted as press ready. The per shade card pictures are cut from the already graded shade masters on the imaging surface, so no pixels are invented for the run and the picture column binds through the verified additionalImageFiles route. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, a real HTML table imports as a live table with per cell background shapes and per cell text, external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded as image data, and the right anchored auto sized wrapper failure and the un inherited font weight are both designed against. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography blows past the inline threshold immediately, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self contained source. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end, and the non standard numeric weights, the display cut by family slug rule and the kebab css_stack rule are all live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only because long queries return zero hits, the orientation filter is broken and never passed, isGenTech is exposed so generated results can be excluded, licensing returns genuine camera scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve placement cap where a 201 means partial success with a failed items list. VOLUME: sixteen client image files plus the card template PDF and the merge CSV in, roughly fifty artefacts moved in total, every multi image call at or under the ten item cap and no batch above twenty, and the seven shade card run is one record per page, well within the merge limits. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no AI object removal, no background replace by prompt, no from scratch image generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
